tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces APG as an auto-parts supply chain governance tool: inventory analytics, cloud snapshots, AIR/SEA ordering, multi-level approvals, monthly data merge and four user roles. It is the map for everything that follows. CLAUDE.md adds working conventions for contributors.

tour.title: Entry Point and App Shell
tour.description: index.tsx mounts React and wraps the tree in providers, then App.tsx acts as the shell: it owns the loaded inventory data, routing between pages and global modals. Starting here shows how every later page is reached.
tour.languageLesson: React composition: index.tsx renders <App/> inside context providers, so any descendant can read auth or i18n state with a hook instead of prop drilling.

tour.title: Domain Types
tour.description: types/inventory.ts is imported by 88 files, making it the shared vocabulary (SKUs, LOIS groups, order and snapshot shapes). Approval and ordering types extend it. Read these first and the rest of the code becomes much easier to follow.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript interfaces and union types give compile-time contracts: a single widely imported types file keeps 88 modules consistent without runtime cost.

tour.title: Auth, Settings and Shared Services
tour.description: authContext provides the signed-in user and role (Admin/Planner/Approver/Viewer), AuthGuard protects routes, and appSettings stores tunable parameters. i18n and validation are small shared utilities used across pages. Together they form the cross-cutting foundation of the shell.

tour.title: CSV Ingestion
tour.description: Daily inventory CSVs enter through FileUpload, which hands them to csvParser and the csv/ helpers and parsers. Parsing normalizes columns before the engine runs, and exporters write results back out. Tests in utils/__tests__ pin down the tricky parsing rules.

tour.title: Inventory Analytics Engine
tour.description: inventoryEngine.ts computes MOS, ROP, stock max, safety stock and LOIS grouping from the parsed rows, using helpers like safetyStock, demandPattern, demandForecast and calendar. It runs inside a Web Worker via inventoryWorker and useInventoryWorker so the UI stays responsive on ~80k SKUs. Results flow into hooks such as useInventoryAnalytics.
tour.languageLesson: Web Workers run CPU-heavy code off the main thread; data is exchanged by message passing (types/worker.d.ts types the messages), so the engine never blocks rendering.

tour.title: Dashboard and Demand Intelligence
tour.description: Dashboard shows stock distribution, trends and LOIS rows built on the engine output, while DemandIntelligence adds forecasting and risk views. Executive reporting and decision-support hooks turn the numbers into actionable summaries.

tour.title: Ordering and Suggestions
tour.description: Ordering is the largest page: planners build AIR/SEA orders with suggested quantities, review drafts, and submit for approval. Supporting charts, warning confirmation, split-draft logic and print templates support the workflow. SkuDetail drills into a single part.

tour.title: Approval Workflow
tour.description: Orders move through brand-specific multi-level approvals. approval-rules and approval-validation encode who may approve what and which status transitions are legal, ApprovalQueue is the approver UI, and hooks handle auth and notifications. Optimistic locking and audit trails are enforced again in the database.

tour.title: Supabase Data Access Layer
tour.description: utils/supabase/ is a facade (index.ts) over focused modules: client, snapshots, monthly-data, approval, profiles, workflows, supersession and storage. Snapshots are gzip-compressed with column pruning and hash dedup before upload. Pages never call Supabase directly, which keeps persistence swappable and testable.

tour.title: Database Schema and Policies
tour.description: Migrations define profiles, approval_requests, audit actions, snapshot and monthly tables plus supersession and part-affinity tables. Triggers enforce sequential approval levels and status transitions, and RLS policies restrict data by role and brand. These rules back the client code from earlier steps.
tour.languageLesson: Row Level Security attaches per-row access predicates to a table, so Postgres itself rejects forbidden reads and writes even if client code is bypassed. Migrations are numbered so the schema evolves in order.

tour.title: Backorders, Transfers and Supersession
tour.description: Further modules extend the core: BackorderAnalytics with aging and velocity matrices, the inter-dealer transfer engine with smart filters and export, supersession chains for replaced part numbers, and part-affinity pairing. Each follows the same pattern of page, hook, pure engine and Supabase module.

tour.title: Edge Functions, Build, CI and Tests
tour.description: Supabase Edge Functions handle privileged tasks such as creating users, resetting passwords, escalation checks, approval emails and a Gemini proxy. Vite, Vitest and the GitHub CI workflow build and verify the app, and Vercel hosts it. Unit tests cover the engine, parsers and approval rules.
